title: Lamine Yamal, Barcelona taking inspiration from LeBron James for Champions League comeback
content:
Lamine Yamal and the Barcelona squad are taking inspiration from LeBron James and the Cleveland Cavaliers’ historic comeback in the 2016 NBA Finals as they attempt to overturn a first-leg deficit in the Champions League.

The Cavaliers became the first team in NBA Finals history to rally from 3-1 down to win a championship with their comeback against the Golden State Warriors ten years ago, with James named the Finals’ Most Valuable Player.

Barcelona trail Atletico Madrid 2-0 in their Champions League quarter-final following last week’s defeat at Camp Nou.

“He (James) is one of my references that can inspire me for tomorrow’s game,” Yamal told a press conference on Monday. “I’ll think about how he did the comeback and I hope it unfolds the same way for me. We have plenty of leaders in the team. I consider myself one of them, but not the only one.”

In the build up to Tuesday’s return leg at the Metropolitano Stadium, the popular internet meme of James wearing sunglasses and headphones, accompanied by a live news caption reading: “No team in NBA finals history has come back from trailing 3-1 (0-32)”, has been doing the rounds on social media. A number of Barcelona players have been edited into a similar pose, accompanied by the caption: “FC Barcelona has never beaten Atletico Madrid in the UCL over 2 legs”.

Sources close to the dressing room, speaking on the condition of anonymity, indicated the Barcelona squad have bought into the social media trend and have been sending these memes to one another as they prepare for the second leg of their quarter-final in Madrid.

On Sunday evening, Yamal, 18, changed his profile picture on Instagram to one of James with the NBA championship and finals’ MVP trophy.

The Golden State Warriors had set an NBA record with 73 regular season wins in 2016, and led the Cleveland Cavaliers 3-1 in the 2016 NBA Finals.

No NBA team in the 70-year history of the league had come back from such a deficit in the Finals, but the Cavaliers recovered and recorded a 93-89 victory in Game 7 to secure the franchise’s first NBA championship.

In Game 7, James recorded 27 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists in what the New York Times described as “one of the most remarkable individual performances in finals history”.

The latest round of La Liga fixtures left Barcelona in pole position to defend their league title, as they extended their lead at the top to nine points after beating Espanyol 4-1, while Real Madrid were held to a draw by Girona.

However, the club’s priority is to win the Champions League over La Liga and Tuesday’s game against Atletico is considered their most important of the season so far.

After Saturday’s victory over Espanyol, the players performed a lap of honour around Camp Nou, which they do not usually do, while the crowd chanted, “Yes we can” in unison — in reference to the second leg against Atletico.

Barcelona lost 2-0 to Atletico in the quarter-final first leg following goals from Julian Alvarez and Alexander Sorloth, with Hansi Flick’s side playing the entirety of the second half with 10 players after Pau Cubarsi’s red card.

“What I can promise for tomorrow is that if we get knocked out, it will be with us fighting until the end,” Yamal said on Monday. “We won’t stop running for one minute and give everything for this badge. I think the comeback is possible.”

Barcelona and Atletico have met twice before in the Champions League quarter-finals, in 2013-14 and 2015-16, and — despite Barca being historically the more successful club — Atletico came out on top on both occasions.

Atletico also staved off an attempted Barca comeback in this season’s Copa de Rey semi-finals. Diego Simeone’s side won the first leg 4-0 and Barca fell just short with a 3-0 second-leg victory.
